subject_line: Five generations of recipes in Praisesong for the Kitchen Ghosts
email_body:
Dear Crystal,

Praisesong for the Kitchen Ghosts moves between poetry, prose and fiction while carrying recipes from five generations of your family, and it was striking to learn it was your first book of nonfiction.

I'd love to ask how you decided which family stories belonged beside which recipes.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. The portrait is developed through a few written questions, which you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Book blends poetry, prose, fiction and recipes from five generations; her first nonfiction (NYT interview republished by UK A&S; UK feature). University email seen in search result of UK-hosted CV (dated 2021).

subject_line: Sheriff Winston Barnes and the plane on the Carolina coast
email_body:
Dear Wiley,

In When Ghosts Come Home, a plane crash on the North Carolina coast pulls Sheriff Winston Barnes into a murder investigation. Congratulations on the 2025 North Carolina Award for Literature.

I'd be curious to ask how Winston's voice first came to you, and how the Roanoke retelling you're working on is taking shape.

book_title: Junah at the End of the World
subject_line: Junah's shoebox time capsule before Y2K
email_body:
Dear Dan,

Junah at the End of the World follows a seventh-grader in Upstate South Carolina in 1999, handed a shoebox time capsule while wondering whether the world will end in December. The vignettes make the book feel like the capsule itself.

I'd like to ask how that fragmentary form came about in your first novel.
